deploy-bot: [DEPLOY START] env=staging user=laura commit=3f2a9c tag=v0.32.1 changewindow=2h. Canary plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Release notes: minor perf + batching fix. CI: green. Logs: https://ci.internal/3456
laura: kicking off smoke now, I'll watch latency and error budget for first 10m :eyes:
raj: noted. can we pin DB migration toggle if any schema flags present? @laura
sam: seeing initial canary -> 10% is fine, metrics look clean so far
deploy-bot: canary progressed: 10% -> 50% (timestamp=3470011245)
sam: on 50% I'm seeing a burst of 502s from svc-inference behind the batcher, rolling traffic back to 10% to reduce blast radius
laura: thanks sam. hold traffic and gather logs. can you paste the top error?
sam: logs snippet: ```ERROR Batcher: allocation failed: OOM when trying to allocate 256MB```
maria: that matches a sequence-length spike we saw in replay. batcher prefetch size might be too aggressive for this workload. opening a follow-up ticket
raj: proposal: roll back that canary to previous tag while we investigate. pin to v0.32.0 for staging to keep tests stable
laura: agree. please run rollback and pin. I'll annotate the rollout thread and notify QA
deploy-bot: [CANARY PAUSED] env=staging reason=502s_from_svc-inference action=hold
deploy-bot: initiating rollback to tag=v0.32.0 commit=1b9c4f (rollback triggered by laura)
laura: confirm rollback started, monitoring logs for recovered 200s
sam: rollback completed on 3/3 nodes, final traffic=100%->v0.32.0
laura: verified baseline returned. 95th latency back to normal, error rate dropped to pre-deploy levels :white_check_mark:
maria: filing postmortem draft: https://wiki.internal/INC-2026-staging-batcher-oom
raj: good catch. we should add a quick safety check for sequence-length distribution before next rollout
deploy-bot: [DEPLOY COMPLETE] env=staging result=rolled-back start_ts=3470011223 end_ts=3470011290 final_tag=v0.32.0 notes="rollback after canary 50% due to svc-inference 502s"
laura: noted and closing this thread. we'll schedule a fix and a follow-up canary once addressed.
